sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- the interception] The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted and destroyed two drones launched by the Ansar Allah toward the Makkah and southern regions on Wednesday Nov 11. Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Maliki announced the interception in a post on X, without details on location, damage or casualties (Arab News 19:40 AST; Sabq 17:05Z; APA 21:23 ; Khaleej Times live blog 20:32 ). Al Jazeera's liveblog (updated 17:45Z = 21:45 ) carries it as: 'The Saudi-led coalition says it has intercepted and destroyed cruise missiles and two drones launched by the Ansar Allah.' [VERIFIED FACT -- same-day second salvo] Earlier Wednesday the coalition said three Ansar Allah cruise missiles toward the Riyadh region were intercepted (recorded 1900-03). Wednesday's total toward Saudi Arabia is therefore FIVE projectiles (3 cruise missiles + 2 drones), all reported intercepted. Tuesday Nov 10 was a DIFFERENT salvo: 1 ballistic + 1 cruise missile toward Riyadh + 1 ballistic missile toward the south. Do not combine the days' figures. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- the holy-city question] The drones were aimed at the Makkah region -- Islam's holiest city -- per the coalition. The Ansar Allah have repeatedly denied targeting the holy cities, saying their operations aim only at Saudi oil facilities and military bases (standing denial, restated after the Nov 6 Makkah drone; Siasat Nov 11 carries Saree's denial without a fresh timestamp -- treat as the standing denial, NOT a confirmed fresh statement on today's two drones). No Ansar Allah claim of today's launches was found in-window. [CONTEXT -- pattern] This is the third Makkah-region drone claim in 18 days: Oct 24 two ballistic missiles toward Makkah/Madinah regions (debris Jeddah-Taif); Nov 6 (Friday) one drone over the Makkah region; Nov 11 two drones. GCC Secretary-General Al-Budaiwi called the October attacks a 'grave violation of the sanctity of the Holy Sites'. [RE-DATE TRAPS -- do not merge] The Al Jazeera edgeone piece at /news/2026/10/30/ ('Saudi Arabia reports interception of Ansar Allah drone targeting Mecca', Friday morning) and the Aaj English Nov 6 piece are the NOV 6 single-drone event, NOT today's two drones. The Roya News denial piece quotes a Ansar Allah political-bureau tweet dated September 16, 2026 -- its denial is not fresh evidence on today's drones.
sections.what_verified: 3 distinct tiered publisher families: Saudi-led coalition statement itself (T1, STATE SA -- primary source), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2, STATE QA), Arab News (T3). Sabq, Siasat, APA and Khaleej Times carry the same announcement but have NO declared tier in the registry and therefore never count toward corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: The Ansar Allah deny targeting Makkah/Madinah (standing denial via military spokesman Yahya Saree and political-bureau member Hizam al-Asad); they say their operations target Saudi oil facilities and military bases only. No Ansar Allah statement claiming today's two drone launches was found. No launch location, debris, damage or casualty detail from any source. The coalition did not identify the drones' launch point.
sections.why_matters: Second Ansar Allah salvo at Saudi Arabia in one day: 3 cruise missiles at Riyadh in the morning, 2 drones at Makkah by evening -- 5 projectiles, all intercepted. Holy-city targeting is the fault line; the denial-vs-claim split is the engagement question.

totw_analysis: Our read: Second Ansar Allah salvo at Saudi Arabia in one day: 3 cruise missiles at Riyadh in the morning, 2 drones at Makkah by evening -- 5 projectiles, all intercepted. Holy-city targeting is the fault line; the denial-vs-claim split is the engagement question. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Did the Ansar Allah really aim drones at Mecca -- or is Riyadh inventing holy-city attacks? The coalition says two drones were destroyed over Makkah; the Ansar Allah deny ever targeting the holy cities.
